source_document.body:
Improving existing wind power facilities, and developing larger and better new installations, is driving the sector’s expansion.
The global market for wind power continues to grow, even as some countries scale back their former targets for wind energy due to policy shifts and other issues. China is still the leading country when it comes to deploying wind energy; various reports utilizing government and other data sources show China’s total installed wind power generation capacity was at least 640 GW at the end of 2025.
The World Wind Energy Association earlier this year said China has an overall share of more than half of the world’s wind power capacity. The agency said China accounted for 77% of global wind power additions in 2025—installing about 130 GW—though growth outside China was mixed, with just five of the top 30 countries for wind power generation capacity showing gains above the global average.
The Global Wind Energy Council (GWEC) recently reported that five wind turbine manufacturers had topped 100 GW of installed generation capacity as of year-end 2025. The leaders include Denmark’s Vestas, which with more than 201 GW of installed capacity was the first turbine manufacturer to pass the 200-GW milestone. Other top manufacturers are China’s Goldwind, Spain-headquartered Siemens Gamesa, U.S.-based GE Vernova, and China’s Envision.
The GWEC in its annual Global Wind Market Development Supply Side Data Report said global wind turbine original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) installed 28,395 new turbines worldwide in 2025, an increase of 23% from 2024. A report from Wood Mackenzie earlier this year said the U.S. wind sector installed more than 8 GW of wind power capacity in 2025, up 49% over the prior year. The group in its US Wind Energy Monitor said the U.S. is expected to install about 11 GW of new wind power capacity in 2026.
Ben Blackwell, CEO of GWEC, earlier this year noted the achievements for the wind power industry and acknowledged continued challenges for the sector. “This impressive growth comes despite years of challenging business conditions and supply chain disruptions and is a testament of the wind sector’s growing importance as a source of reliable, homegrown renewable energy at a time of turmoil in international import-based oil and gas markets,” said Blackwell. “We now have five companies that have each installed more than 100 GW, which is enough electricity to power many of the world’s largest economies. But this is only just the beginning. With wind power meeting 9.5% of global electricity demand today, we see enormous potential for wind manufacturers from all regions to continue to expand and grow their operations across existing and emerging markets.”
Onshore and Offshore
Energy industry analysts continue to tout the advantages of wind power, while differentiating between onshore wind and offshore wind. Onshore wind is faster to build and cheaper to maintain than offshore wind, and is considered among the most affordable renewable energy resources, similar to solar power. The intermittent generation of onshore wind is a talking point, though, as is its visual and aesthetic impact. Offshore wind (Figure 1) is considered more efficient than onshore locations because winds at sea are usually steadier and stronger—but opponents of offshore installations also cite their environmental impacts on marine and avian ecosystems.
1. Offshore wind installations are considered more efficient than onshore sites because winds at sea are usually steadier and stronger than winds over land. Courtesy: Envato / Image-Source
Much of the focus in the wind sector is tied to equipment manufacturing, including ever-larger turbines for both onshore and offshore installations. Sustainability is part of the discussion as well, with advancements focused on the circular economy and a drive to create fully recyclable turbine blades. Wind power sites, similar to the solar power industry, also now increasingly include energy storage so that excess power can be stored and then discharged into the power grid when needed.
Tapas Peshin, who holds a PhD in Energy Resources Engineering from Stanford University, and is Product Lead, Transmission & Reliability, with PCI Energy Solutions, talked with POWER about some of the challenges for today’s wind energy sector.
“Wind’s reliability problem is mostly a geography problem,” said Peshin. “The wind is almost always blowing somewhere. The question is whether the grid can move that energy across a wide enough area and schedule it a day ahead. Regional day-ahead markets in the West, such as SPP Markets+ [Southwest Power Pool’s services that centralize day-ahead and real-time unit commitment and dispatch] and CAISO’s EDAM [California Independent System Operator’s Extended Day-Ahead Market], matter for wind because they widen the footprint over which variability averages out.”
Peshin, like other industry experts who spoke with POWER , said pairing wind power with energy storage is of significant importance. “Storage paired with wind is less about holding power for days and more about shaping it. A battery that can shift a few hours of overnight wind into the evening peak makes that wind something an operator can actually commit to, not just a forecast,” said Peshin, who also noted how transmission constraints impact wind power.
“The binding constraint on wind is rarely the turbines,” said Peshin. “It’s transmission. A wind project without firm transmission and a clear scheduling path will be curtailed exactly when it’s producing the most, which undercuts both its economics and its climate value.”
Juan Pablo (JP) Cerda, CEO and co-founder of Renewabl, a UK-based climate tech and renewable energy company, told POWER that wind power’s reliability should not be underestimated. “For a buyer, reliability is a count of hours: how many of the year’s 8,760 [hours] does your contracted generation cover? Wind lifts that count because it generates at night and rarely drops at the same time as solar—in the UK, IRENA [International Renewable Energy Agency], citing Ember, puts days when both are low at only 2% of the time. Storage covers the rest by moving the midday surplus into the hours you are short, and the market does not pay for that shift yet.”
Cerda also said wind power can help with the challenge of energy demand from data centers. “A data center draws a flat load around the clock, so an annual renewable total hides the night hours,” said Cerda. “Wind is the main technology that covers them: in our German data center modeling, solar alone covers 41% of hours and wind alone 75% at the same annual volume, so for a flat load the technology mix is the biggest lever. At Renewabl we measure that hourly baseline for corporates and data centers, then run the tenders that move it.”
Technology Advancements
The evolution of wind turbines has brought ever-larger equipment to market in recent years, both for offshore and onshore installations. Mingyang, a Chinese company, is developing a 33-MW offshore wind turbine, according to a document distributed at a recent wind power event in China. At present, the world’s largest-capacity offshore wind turbine is the Dongfang DEW-26 MW-310 (Figure 2), built by Dongfang Electric Corp. in China. The 26-MW unit features a 310-meter rotor diameter and a 185-meter hub height, comparable to the height of a 60-story building. The tallest wind turbine, though, is considered to be GICON’s 365-meter-tall unit, built in Germany by GICON and Sprind. It has just 3.8 MW of generation capacity, but uses a steel lattice support structure combined with a telescoping inner tower to reach nearly 1,200 feet in height—taller than the Eiffel Tower in Paris, France.
2. The Dongfang DEW-26 MW-310, built by Dongfang Electric Corp. in China, is to date the largest offshore wind turbine in the world. The turbine entered commercial operation in late October 2025 in Dongying, in East China’s Shandong Province. Source: Chinese government news release/sasac.gov.cn
Mingyang has also developed the MySE 22-MW offshore wind turbine, which features a rotor diameter of more than 310 meters and is engineered to resist severe typhoon conditions. Siemens Gamesa’s SG DD-276 is an offshore turbine rated at 21.5 MW and with a 276-meter rotor diameter. Mingyang’s equipment also includes the MySE 18.X-20 MW, with a rated output in the 18- to 20-MW range, with rotor diameters ranging from 260 meters to 292 meters (853 feet to 958 feet). It is designed for offshore environments and features anti-typhoon technologies.
Dongfang also has developed the DEW-18 MW-260, rated 18 MW with a rotor diameter of 260 meters. Goldwind has a GWH252-16 MW turbine that has a rotor diameter of 252 meters. Vestas’ portfolio features the V236-15.0 MW offshore turbine, which has a 236-meter rotor diameter.
The largest onshore wind turbine is considered to be the 15-MW Sany SI-270150, developed by China’s Sany Group. Other Chinese manufacturers, including Envision, Goldwind, and Windey, have models ranging from 7.7 MW to 10 MW of generation capacity. Industry analysts have said that larger turbines, capable of producing more energy and in turn doing so more efficiently, also could be key for powering data centers—a point made often by those who spoke with POWER .
“A fascinating fact is that the companies most involved in the AI [artificial intelligence] infrastructure buildout are those most committed to sustainability goals. And the need for unprecedented amounts of power for data centers is turbocharging the hunger for clean power,” said Jay Ruckelshaus, PhD, co-founder and head of Partnerships & Policy at Gravity, a company that helps customers cut energy costs and support sustainability through cost and emissions reductions. “The companies doing this well treat clean energy procurement as part of their energy strategy, not as a separate line item for sustainability. For data centers, like other industries, reliability is increasingly of concern. For most operators, a portfolio approach is key. Wind can contribute electrons when solar output drops, and vice versa—and both can be supplemented by increasingly economical storage options. When those projects are new, they add supply to the grid.
“There’s a natural alliance between being smart with your energy spend and being smart with your emissions,” said Ruckelshaus. “Every ounce of power a data center saves through better cooling or more efficient computing doesn’t have to be generated, so each new wind project covers more of the load and there’s less strain on the grid at peak times. The cheapest and cleanest kilowatt hour is still the one you never have to buy. Moreover, as power prices rise in many markets, the marginal value of energy efficiency is growing.”
Sustainability, Reliability, Flexibility
Grid integration of renewable energy is often part of discussions about system flexibility, because the output from renewables such as wind changes depending on weather and time of day. Several of those who spoke with POWER noted that wind energy can present a complex engineering challenge because weather patterns are ever-changing. Wind speeds are not constant, so wind energy cannot be relied on for baseload power. Integrating energy storage, though, means excess electricity can be saved and then discharged to the grid as needed. Pairing wind with other renewable resources, including solar and hydropower, can create a stronger generation profile. And advanced weather forecasting methods, supported by AI and real-time meteorological data, is allowing electric utilities and grid operators to better predict wind profiles at times days in advance.
Paul Hines, vice president and chief scientist with EnergyHub, a group that supports utilities in managing load growth and virtual power plants, told POWER flexibility is of increasing importance to maintaining grid reliability and balancing electricity supply and demand, particularly as more wind energy comes online.
“Wind has an important role to play in meeting growing electricity demand. In many regions, it complements solar by producing more electricity during evening and overnight hours when solar isn’t generating,” said Hines. “Wind production also varies with wind speed, which creates an operational challenge for a grid that needs to balance electricity supply and demand every second of every day.
“As more wind and solar generation comes online, maintaining that balance requires that we add flexibility to the grid to move power away from times of plenty to times of scarcity,” said Hines. “Historically, grid operators have relied heavily on dispatchable fossil generation [primarily natural gas] to respond to changes in demand. Today, resources like batteries, EVs [electric vehicles], and smart thermostats give utilities more options for adjusting electricity consumption based on available generation.
“Two capabilities are especially important as the generation mix evolves: forecasting and demand flexibility,” said Hines. “Accurate forecasts help grid operators anticipate changes in wind production, while demand flexibility allows them to respond by shifting consumption or dispatching flexible resources when needed. Together, they help utilities make better use of renewable generation while maintaining reliability and managing costs.”
Carolyn Kissane, associate dean of the New York University (NYU) School of Professional Studies (SPS) Center for Global Affairs, told POWER , “Wind power can advance sustainability and energy security by generating electricity without fuel combustion or exposure to volatile fuel prices, a problem around the world today. Its contribution to reliability depends on the system.”
3. Where wind farms are located is key to their output and efficiency. Most onshore installations are in more rural areas, where the open land is conducive to greater wind speeds. Courtesy: Envato / PedaltotheStock
Kissane, founding director of the SPS Energy, Climate Justice, and Sustainability Lab, added, “Pairing wind with storage helps manage fluctuations and shift electricity to periods of greater demand. Transmission, geographic diversity, and complementary generation remain essential, particularly during prolonged periods of low wind. Wind is best placed in geographies with strong wind speeds [Figure 3].”
Mike Mohamed, head of Energy Transition at Solomon Partners, a New York City-headquartered investment bank that works with clients in the infrastructure, power, and renewable sector, along with other industries, said pairing wind power with energy storage is important to ensure a reliable supply of power.
“As wind is intermittent and energy storage is instantaneously dispatchable, storage can be used as a short-term bridge tool to smooth out minute fluctuations of wind output to ensure a consistent and reliable stream of energy,” said Mohamed. “Furthermore, during periods of excess wind production, storage can charge from the wind asset and wait on standby for periods of low or non-existent wind in order to extend the wind asset’s deployment window.”
The Data Center Question
Wind energy may not be the first choice of many data center operators when it comes to finding a power supply, but its use is increasing in importance, especially among companies looking to lower carbon emissions. Analysts told POWER that one modern wind turbine can produce as much power as tens of thousands of solar panels, with the potential to produce energy day and night. Wind power also can help stabilize energy costs; siting data centers near wind farms or co-locating them with behind-the-meter renewable energy assets can protect against grid price volatility.
4. Wind turbines spin near Google’s Eemshaven, Netherlands, data center. Courtesy: Google
Mohamed said wind power can be important for data center operators to support their need for electricity (Figure 4). “Wind projects tend to be large in size and are typically located in rural communities,” he said, and noted such installations can “provide sufficient power and ample space for large data center builds. However, as wind is an intermittent resource, it must be used as part of a comprehensive energy strategy that pairs wind generation alongside batteries and backup conventional generation resources.”
Mohamed told POWER , “Wind paired with solar tends to complement each other quite well as peak production windows are often staggered, providing a longer-term, lower-carbon energy supply. Select data center owners have started to pursue acquisitions of operating wind farms as they provide an immediate ability to draw on power at scale.”
Kissane said that “for data centers, buying wind power is part of a broader strategy to secure dependable, less carbon-intensive electricity. In some cases, companies buy credits to support wind projects that do not directly connect to their project but are important for reducing their overall emissions footprint.”
Said Ruckelshaus, “The Electric Power Research Institute projects that data centers could use between 9% and 17% of U.S. electricity by 2030, up from about 4%–5% today. That’s a big new load for the grid, and the Department of Energy has pointed to land-based wind, along with solar, storage, and efficiency, as some of the fastest and most cost-competitive ways to meet it.
“Data center operators are also exactly the kind of buyer clean energy project developers need: large, creditworthy, and ready to commit to buying power for many years,” said Ruckelshaus. “When an operator agrees to take the output of a new wind farm for a decade or more, that contract is often what gets the project financed and built.”
Hines said, “The grid needs a tremendous amount of additional capacity, and it needs it quickly. Data centers, manufacturing, EVs [electric vehicles], and heat pumps are all contributing to growing electricity demand. Meeting this demand while maintaining reliability, keeping electricity affordable, and limiting emissions will require utilities to make the most of every available resource.
“Wind and solar are essential parts of that equation,” said Hines. “In the right locations, they can be deployed relatively quickly to help meet growing demand. Although their output varies with weather conditions, storage and flexible demand help manage that variability by shifting consumption to low-demand periods and injecting power when needed. Forecasting is equally important because it allows grid operators to anticipate when renewable generation will be available and plan accordingly.
“The opportunity is to coordinate these resources rather than manage them independently. When wind generation is abundant, utilities can shift flexible consumption into those hours,” said Hines. “When renewable output is expected to decline or demand is approaching a peak, batteries and other distributed resources can help reduce pressure on the grid. New generation and infrastructure investments are necessary, but utilities also need to make better use of the capacity already available. Coordinating renewable generation, storage, and flexible demand can help accommodate growing loads while managing costs and emissions.”
Repowering
Repowering of wind energy projects is a major step for supporting sustainability in the sector, and increasing the ongoing reliability of installations. Exus Renewables North America in September marked commercial operation of its Highland North and Cambria wind repower projects in Pennsylvania. The company noted that completion of the repowerings comes as demand for clean power from data centers and other large energy users continues to climb in the area. Exus officials said Cambria’s output is contracted under a signed power purchase agreement with a Fortune 500 technology company, noting that a growing number of corporate power buyers are turning to repowered wind sites for capacity that can come online without the multi-year interconnection timeline a new project requires.
“Highland North and Cambria show what repowering can deliver: proven wind resources, established infrastructure, and a faster path to new capacity,” said Jim Spencer, president and CEO of Exus Renewables North America, at a ceremony marking completion of the projects. “Completing both projects is a milestone for our Pennsylvania portfolio and for the communities that have supported this work.”
Cambria, a 61.6-MW facility, initially came online in 2008. Highland North, with 75 MW of capacity, first entered service in 2012. The projects together bring Exus’ owned wind power generation capacity in Pennsylvania to 306.9 MW. Vestas supplied the turbines for both projects, with JMS Energy serving as balance of plant contractor. Some $356 million in construction financing was led by KeyBanc Capital Markets. The repower replaced each turbine’s nacelle, blades, and generator on the existing towers and foundations, extending operating life another 30 years.
Seth Wilmore, vice president of Wind and Energy Transition at Exus, told POWER , “Finding efficiencies inside an industry that is already efficient means looking hard at how we treat the assets we’ve built. Repowering is one of the clearest examples. When we repower a wind project, we’re getting more clean energy out of a site that already has the land, the interconnection, and the community relationships in place, which is about as efficient as development gets. To date, we’ve repowered over 516 MW of wind projects.”
Wilmore continued, “What happens to the old equipment matters too, and as an industry we have more work to do there. Recycling options for blades and panels aren’t where they need to be yet. At our Twin Ridges repower, we partnered with Carbon Rivers to upcycle the fiberglass blades and keep them out of the landfill, and at our Highland North and Cambria wind repower projects, we donated one of the retired nacelles to the Universal Technical Institute Inc. in San Antonio [Texas] so students could train on real equipment. Those are steps in the right direction. We’re continuing to look for options that make sense on future projects, because the long-term credibility of renewables depends on getting end of life right.”
5. KK Group, headquartered in Denmark, said it recently secured its first U.S. wind farm repowering contract. The company said it will provide targeted repowering through converter control upgrades. Courtesy: KK Group
KK Group, a Denmark-headquartered company with offices in 10 countries (including a dedicated U.S. regional division based in Houston, Texas), in October announced it had secured its first repowering order (Figure 5) in the U.S. The company, formerly known as KK Wind Solutions, in a news release wrote, “As U.S. grid requirements evolve, aging control technology makes it increasingly challenging to keep older wind turbines connected. KK Group will provide targeted repowering through converter control upgrades on 33 GE 1.5-MW turbines for a U.S. utility, helping extend the generating life of the existing assets.” The company continued, “By replacing aging converter controls with KK Group’s upgraded technology, the utility will be able to keep its existing turbines operating while supporting compliance with current grid requirements.”
Kim Wichmann-Hansen, president of KK Group US, said, “Replacing a wind turbine that still has years of productive life ahead of it doesn’t always make sense. But keeping older turbines operating also means ensuring their technology can meet the requirements of today’s electricity grid. By upgrading the controls, we can help operators bridge that gap and get more value from assets they already have.”
Wichmann-Hansen told POWER , “As the global wind fleet ages, extending the productive life of existing turbines—and therefore the amount of renewable energy produced—will become increasingly important to reducing the environmental impact of the industry. Repair, refurbishment, and targeted repowering all have an important role to play. By repairing or upgrading critical components, rather than replacing them unnecessarily, operators can extend turbine lifetime while reducing demand for new materials, manufacturing, and associated emissions.
“The opportunity is to make repair and refurbishment a more integral part of wind turbine maintenance, bringing these capabilities closer to where turbines operate,” said Wichmann-Hansen. “This can help reduce transport-related emissions, shorten repair times, and keep existing wind assets generating reliably for longer. For power electronics and control systems, our experience shows that on-site refurbishment can reduce lifecycle emissions by up to 95% compared with replacement.”
KK Group’s CMC1 Converter Controller is at the center of its U.S. project. The converter controller helps manage how electricity generated by the turbine is converted and delivered to the grid. By replacing the older controller while retaining the existing converter and other major turbine infrastructure, the solution provides a targeted way to modernize the turbine without replacing major components that can continue operating, according to the company. KK Group said that to expand the application of CMC1 across different converter systems, it is working with power electronics specialist ZOPF to develop interface technology that enables the controller to integrate with existing converter hardware.
“Wind turbines are designed to operate for decades, but technology and grid requirements continue to evolve. Even when major turbine components remain operational, aging control systems can make it increasingly difficult to maintain reliable operations and meet current grid requirements,” said Wichmann-Hansen. “Targeted repowering addresses this challenge by upgrading critical technology while retaining infrastructure that can continue operating. This helps operators manage technological obsolescence, support grid compliance, and extend the reliable operation of existing wind assets.
“Our first U.S. repowering project is a good example of this approach. We are upgrading converter control technology on 33 GE 1.5-MW turbines, helping a U.S. utility extend the operating life of its existing assets without replacing major components unnecessarily,” said Wichmann-Hansen. “With a large and aging installed wind fleet in the U.S., we see significant potential for targeted repowering, alongside monitoring, maintenance, and repair, to support a more reliable and sustainable wind industry. In short, we put today’s knowledge into yesterday’s turbines—to ensure they also operate tomorrow.”
Equipment Recycling
Energy industry analysts often point to equipment recycling as a key element of sustainability in the renewable energy space; wind power is no different. The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) has said about 85% to 90% of the mass of a wind turbine is made of materials that can already be commercially recycled. The agency said most of the unrecycled materials include fiber-reinforced composites such as carbon fiber and fiberglass (Figure 6), which are found in wind turbine blades, nacelle covers, and the cover for the hub that connects the blades to the wind turbine.
6. Carbon Rivers, with funding from the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE), demonstrated a pyrolysis process that recovered glass fiber at 99.9% purity from several end-of-life waste streams, including wind turbine blades. Source: DOE / Carbon Rivers
Critical minerals used in the wind energy industry, including rare earth elements from the neodymium and dysprosium magnets used in generators, also do not have commercial-scale recycling options, according to the DOE.
There are, though, several ongoing recycling efforts. Leon Mishnaevsky Jr., a professor at the Department of Wind and Energy Systems at Technical University of Denmark (DTU Wind), pointed POWER toward the group’s WISEWIND project. Mishnaevsky Jr. coordinates several projects aligned with sustainability and reliability of wind turbines. He noted that the WISEWIND effort focuses on developing new blade materials designed to “ensure re-processability, easy reparability, and repeated recyclability of blades. [A] new generation of recyclable wind turbine blades, based on vitrimer resins, is developed, on the basis of a digital twin of blade materials ‘from cradle to cradle.’ ”
The WISEWIND consortium includes DTU Wind, Siemens Gamesa Renewable Energy, and ReFlow ApS, an environmental consultancy firm. Mishnaevsky Jr. said that in the project, “various recyclable composites were tested for their application in wind turbine blades, and advanced computational models of their recycling were developed. DTU also organizes a series of bi-annual international conferences on sustainable wind turbine blades, most recently in 2024 and again in 2026.”
Veolia was one of the first companies in the U.S. to recycle wind turbine blades at scale. The company works with OEMs, contractors, and others. The firm’s program involves crews that “cut the large fiberglass blades into manageable sections and run them through industrial shredders and grinders to produce a confetti-like or chunk-sized material.” The company said it is used in cement co-processing, where “the shredded material is sent to partner cement kilns,” and “65% to 75% of the blade material replaces raw silica, limestone, and other minerals in the cement mix… 28% of the material serves as a high-heat alternative fuel source that replaces coal in firing the kiln.”
Veolia has said, “Each processed blade replaces roughly 5 tons of coal, 2.7 tons of silica, 1.9 tons of limestone, and 1 ton of other raw materials… The co-processing method cuts net carbon dioxide (CO 2 ) emissions by about 27% compared to traditional Portland cement manufacturing.”
Among the companies recycling used wind power equipment is Ohio-based Canvus, which takes retired, non-biodegradable fiberglass wind turbine blades and turns them into functional public furniture and art. The Dutch company Blade Made has turned old blades into bus shelters and bicycle storage units; the Port of Aalborg in Denmark is known for its sustainable bicycle shelter built from a decommissioned wind turbine blade. And used blades have been used as noise barriers on interstate highways in the U.S.
Said NYU’s Kissane, “Sustainability [in wind power] also requires planning for retirement… extending equipment life, recovering valuable materials, and scaling recycling for turbine blades.”
— Darrell Proctor is a senior editor for POWER.

This Is It: Robert Pattinson Officially Cast As the Next James Bond
13 photos
Photo: Amazon
This is the moment we have all been waiting for, more than seven years, since Daniel Craig first confirmed his exit in 2019. London-born Robert Pattinson has officially been cast as the next James Bond. Amazon MGM Studios announced the 40-year-old British actor as Daniel Craig's successor.
Robert Pattinson goes from Gotham to MI6, becoming the seventh actor to portray the iconic British spy in the film series, joining an elite cast alongside Sean Connery, George Lazenby, Roger Moore, Timothy Dalton, Pierce Brosnan, and Daniel Craig.
The upcoming James Bond movie will be directed by Dune filmmaker Denis Villeneuve, who previously worked with Robert Pattinson on Dune: Part Three. Peaky Blinders creator Steven Knight is writing the screenplay. Amy Pascal and David Heyman will produce the movie.
Pattinson described inheriting the iconic role as " a dream come true " and " the honor of a lifetime. " This marks the first major casting decision since Amazon MGM Studios took creative control of the franchise and launched its casting search in May 2026. It’s been a roller coaster ride, with names such as Callum Turner, Jack Lowden, and Josh O'Connor being shortlisted for the legendary part. Pattinson was not even part of the initial testing pool.
Photo: MovieStation | YouTube Robert Pattinson was born in London, England, following the tradition of casting British actors or those from Commonwealth nations and Ireland as James Bond, a pattern surprisingly continued by Amazon MGM Studios.
However, Amazon makes a major departure from a long-standing unwritten rule: never cast an actor already famous for another iconic franchise role. The English actor has already starred as Bruce Wayne in The Batman in 2022, Edward Cullen in The Twilight Saga from 2008 through 2012, and Cedric Diggory in Harry Potter and the Goblet of Fire back in 2005.
Pattinson is currently in cinemas playing the real-life television journalist Chris Hansen in the psychological thriller Primetime. He hits the theaters again in December 2026 with the sci-fi sequel Dune: Part Three, where he plays Scytale.
The new 007 was received with open arms by some critics, while others see his casting as a bad idea. The Guardian film critic Peter Bradshaw called him an " exquisite choice ." On the other hand, television broadcaster Piers Morgan publicly criticized the decision, writing that " Batman can't be Bond too. "
Photo: Warner Bros. Pictures | YouTube Amazon MGM Studios has yet to announce the exact release date for Robert Pattinson's first James Bond movie and the 26th installment of the franchise, but it is widely expected to arrive in cinemas sometime in 2028.
However, Amazon should start working on the new James Bond in 2027, once director Denis Villeneuve finishes his promotional tour for Dune. A 2028 release would mark a seven-year gap since Daniel Craig ’s final outing in No Time to Die, which premiered back in September 2021. This is by far the longest hiatus between films in the 007 series. The title of the upcoming installment is still a work in progress.

source_document.body:
A Tesla Model 3 drove into an overturned box truck on I-75 near Naples, Florida, killing two of its passengers and a man who had stopped to help. Tesla’s own report to federal regulators says Autopilot or “Full Self-Driving” was engaged, at 71 mph.
Police and local media covered the May 31 crash as a truck wreck in the dark, and none of it mentioned a driver-assist system. It’s the latest case in our ongoing investigation into fatal crashes hidden in Tesla’s NHTSA data , and it lands as Tesla’s monthly crash count hits another record.
What happened on I-75
Just before 4 a.m. on Sunday, May 31, 2026, the 31-year-old driver of a 2014 Freightliner lost the road near the Pine Ridge Road exit in Collier County, steered back onto southbound I-75, and flipped it, according to the Florida Highway Patrol. The overturned truck ended up blocking the center and outside lanes.
Jonathan Garcia Arias, a 25-year-old Naples man and former Marine, was driving by in a BMW. He pulled over and got out to help the truck driver.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Then a southbound 2023 Tesla with five young men from Naples inside came up on the scene. FHP’s report says the front of the Tesla hit the underside of the overturned truck and Garcia Arias. Two of the Tesla’s passengers, aged 18 and 19, died at the scene, and Garcia Arias died later in the hospital. The 20-year-old driver and two more passengers were seriously hurt.
A few days later, FHP used the crash as a warning about stopping near wrecks on the interstate. Senior Trooper Kenn Watson said the Tesla driver would have seen only the truck’s underside, with “no lights, no reflectors, nothing warning them.”
So that’s the official story. A dark obstacle, a driver who couldn’t see it in time. Nobody said a word about Autopilot.
What Tesla told the federal government
Under NHTSA’s Standing General Order, automakers have to report crashes where a Level 2 driver-assist system was engaged within 30 seconds of impact and someone was killed or hurt. Tesla filed one for this crash.
It identifies the car as a 2023 Model 3 on a highway, flags a traffic incident on the roadway, and marks the automation “Engagement Status” as “Verified Engaged.” That means Tesla confirmed through its own telematics that Autopilot or FSD was on. It logs a pre-crash speed of 71 mph and a fatality, lists the Florida Highway Patrol as the investigating agency, and says it learned of the crash from police and the media.
Then it blacks out the crash narrative, the software version, and whether the road was within the system’s approved operating domain, all as “confidential business information.” That’s the same redaction Tesla applies to 99.9% of its reports .
The report also surfaced late. Tesla filed it as a 5-Day report, the urgent category for fatal crashes, but it didn’t land until Tesla’s September filings, more than three months after the crash. And Tesla lists law enforcement as one of the ways it found out about it.
How we matched it: Tesla logged the incident time as 07:56 UTC, which converts to 3:56 a.m. in Florida, two minutes off the 3:54 a.m. in FHP’s report. The city, the highway, the 2023 model year, the month and the fatal outcome all line up, and it’s the only fatal Tesla driver-assist report in Naples that month. It’s the same crash.
Tesla has been here before
A Tesla on driver-assist going highway speed into the underside of a big truck, in the dark, in Florida. If that sounds familiar, it should.
In 2016, Joshua Brown was killed near Williston when his Model S on Autopilot drove under a tractor-trailer crossing the highway. In 2019, Jeremy Banner died in Delray Beach when his Model 3 on Autopilot went under a trailer at 68 mph and had its roof sheared off. In both crashes, neither the driver nor the system braked.
Trooper Watson’s point was that a human couldn’t see the truck. But a big, unlit obstacle sitting across two lanes at night is exactly the kind of thing a driver-assist system is supposed to catch, and Tesla now sells FSD as nearly ready to drive with nobody watching. And an attentive driver could clearly see it, as the BMW driver did, and stop before the Tesla arrived.
We want to be fair about what the data doesn’t prove. “Engaged within 30 seconds” is the reporting trigger. Tesla’s 71 mph may be a telematics snapshot rather than the impact speed. And with the software version redacted, we can’t say whether this was Autopilot or FSD.
A new record: 264 crashes in September
The NHTSA release that surfaced this crash, covering filings through October 15, also set a new monthly high. Tesla reported 264 driver-assist crashes in September 2026, beating July’s 236, which was itself a record. That’s up from 135 in March.
September may still grow as late reports come in. This Naples crash shows how late they can be.
Our merged dataset now holds 4,669 Tesla driver-assist crash reports since 2019, 69 of them flagged fatal. The same release added two other fatal reports, both “Verified Engaged” and both covered locally with no mention of driver-assist: a Model Y that hit a tree and burned in El Dorado Hills, California, killing three, and a Model X that hit a signal pole in Naples on September 30, killing a passenger. We’ll lay those out separately.
Electrek’s Take
Three people died on I-75, including a man who got out of his car to help a stranger. Tesla knows its driver-assist was on, knows the speed, holds the telematics, and filed a federal report saying so. Then it sealed everything that would explain what the car did, and the public got a story about a dark truck.
Top comment by Aigars Mahinovs
Liked by 16 people
That's what happens when the system has to identify all objects in the camera frame before it can start to estimate the objects position and then relative distance and then relative velocity. Unrecognizable objects will destroy all your logic. This is a design failure and not something Tesla can actually fix.
Compare that to radars and lidars that directly measure distances and relative velocities of everything in front of the car, regardless of what it is. That is a far better approach because you do not want the car the impact objects on its trajectory regardless of what those objects turn out to be.
View all comments
Tesla’s whole pitch for FSD is that the car sees better than you do, and yet, Tesla vehicles on Autopilot and FSD keep crashing on stationary objects on the highway. It’s the same failure that killed Joshua Brown and Jeremy Banner years ago. If the system saw the truck and the driver overrode it, Tesla should say so. It was quick to do that in the Katy crash when the data helped it. If the system didn’t see it, that’s a safety defect regulators and owners need to know about.
Either way, the redaction protects Tesla, not the people on the road. It’s the same pattern we found in Vineland and in July’s four fatal crashes , and the crash count keeps setting records.
We’re asking the Florida Highway Patrol for the full crash report, whether its investigators got Tesla’s raw vehicle data, and whether they even knew the system was engaged. If they didn’t, the only party that knows what this car did is the one that sealed the file.

EICMA 2026 • Honda CRF1150L Africa Twin Enduro Sports Is a Tongue Twister, Weighs Less but Offers More
Massive 1954 Page 721 Dragline Sitting for Decades Walks Again Ahead of Restoration
16 photos
Photo: Scrappy Industries/YouTube
I don't know about you, but I love revival videos. There's something very cool about seeing a classic car spring back to life after sitting for decades. If you're also a fan of such content, I have something special for you today. This revival video is not about a car but a dragline excavator, a large piece of construction equipment.
Yes, it's perhaps a strange thing to see on these pages, but this thing is spectacularly massive. And even though it doesn't have wheels, it does move under its own power. Moreover, this walking dragline is a rare sight, and, following the revival, it became the only one of its kind that's operational.
If you're unfamiliar with dragline (and it's quite alright if that's the case), these heavy-duty excavators emerged in the early 20th century, replacing the steam and power shovels. Unlike standard excavators that push a bucket away from the machine using a hydraulic arm, draglines rely on gravity and wide ropes suspended from a long boom.
Draglines were primarily used in surface mining but were also utilized in major canal projects, dredging, quarries, and civil engineering. Most draglines are replaced by rotary excavators beginning in the 1970s.
Because large draglines are too heavy for tracks or wheels, they move using massive "shoes" on either side. These lift the machine and slide it forward a few feet at a time. The dragline you see here is one of those rigs.
A Page 721 model from 1954, this dragline is directly linked to the man who invented the concept back in the day. That man is John W. Page, who created the first dragline to use in digging the Chicago Canal. Page built the first walking dragline in 1923 and developed the first diesel engine exclusively for dragline use a year later.
Page also invented the arched dragline bucket, which is still commonly used today, while pioneering an archless bucket design in the 1960s. He started his own dragline-building company in 1912.
A medium-sized walking dragline, the Page 721 is about 22 feet (6.7 meters) high, with the tip of its boom sitting at up to 80 feet (24.4 meters) above the ground . With the 125-foot (38-meter) long boom operating at 30 degrees, the overall machine length reaches a whopping 150 feet. It has an operating weight of 325 to 350 short tons (650,000 to 700,000 pounds).
The Page 721 was originally equipped with an in-house-built horizontal V6 engine running at a constant 450 RPM. This dragline, however, had its original mill replaced with a Cummins unit. The 19-liter inline-six diesel powerplant is part of the iconic KT-series family, which became an industry standard for heavy mining in the 1970s.
This walking dragline has been sitting in a sand and gravel pit for about 20 years. This usually means the end of the line for such equipment, but this Page excavator got lucky. The owner decided to donate it to the Historical Construction Equipment Association in Bowling Green, Ohio.
The donating family and the HCEA have an agreement requiring that the association have it running and operating at their grounds, which is why we're witnessing this historic moment. The HCEA sent a team to have Page 721 operating again in order to move it in a position where it could be disassembled.
The dragline would then be moved to Bowling Green piece by piece, with each to be sandblasted and painted before reassembly. When that happens, it will become the only Page 721 in the world that's fully operational. Until that happens, you can see it coming back to life after 20 years in the video below.
And by the way, if you're a fan of old construction equipment, you can donate to help the HCEA move and restore the walking dragline. You can find more info on their website .

The FDA rejected Summit Therapeutics’ ivonescimab over the weekend, sending a strong message to rival drugmakers Bristol Myers Squibb, BioNTech, Pfizer, Merck and AbbVie.
With the rejection of Summit Therapeutics’ PD-1xVEGF therapy, the FDA has drawn a line in the sand, firmly setting improved overall survival as the gold-standard bar for approval in oncology.
Summit submitted the biologics license application for ivonescimab based on evidence from the Phase 3 HARMONi trial that showed an improvement in progression-free survival in patients with EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Originally, the study did not show increased overall survival, but the company followed up in September with additional data that suggested a slight improvement in OS.
But the FDA, evidently, was not convinced. The agency issued a complete response letter (CRL) over the weekend, declaring that substantial evidence of effectiveness had not been established. The PFS improvement on its own did not support a positive benefit-risk profile for the therapy, the FDA concluded.
“At first glance, it’s clear to us that OS matters most, with PFS a nice to have, but not the determinate endpoint,” BMO Capital Markets wrote on Sunday evening.
Ivonescimab combined with chemotherapy in the indication achieved PFS of 6.4 months as compared to 4.4 months in the control arm. OS was 18.6 months compared to 14, which was not statistically significant. The FDA had warned that this would not be enough, but Summit went ahead with the application.
Cancer
Drugmakers rush to pair up with Summit’s ivonescimab ahead of key verdict
With companies including AstraZeneca, Pfizer and Revolution Medicines clamoring to get in on Summit Therapeutics’ Akeso-partnered PD-1xVEGF antibody, one analyst calls the asset “the next major backbone” of cancer treatment.
November 2, 2026
·
6 min read
·
Tristan Manalac
Read more
“Overall survival remains the gold-standard bar in NSCLC: Summit ivonescimab HARMONi CRL is largely unsurprising given FDA’s previously communicated OS requirement,” BMO wrote.
But while BMO was not surprised by the rejection, analysts from Stifel had been more bullish. The firm’s Dara Azar, associate vice president of biotech equity research, told BioSpace earlier this month that the application was unlikely to hit any regulatory snags.
“Today’s CRL appears to indicate the FDA will require robust evidence of survival benefit rather than allowing even substantial PFS improvement to carry a filing when OS is a key endpoint,” BMO wrote.
Not only does this set Summit back on a potential U.S. launch for ivonescimab, which has been hailed as the potential next backbone of oncology treatments, it also puts the biotech’s rivals on notice.
Get the gold
Coming behind Summit in the PD-1xVEGF class are partners Bristol Myers Squibb and BioNTech, plus Pfizer, Merck and AbbVie. These companies could see pressure on shares when the markets open Monday, BMO predicted.
BioNTech in particular will need to take note, the analysts said. The company’s BMS-partnered program for pumitamig is already in Phase 3 testing. Earlier in the clinic are Pfizer with tivunatamig (PF-08634404), Merck’s MK-2010 (LM-299) and AbbVie’s ABBV-1480 (RC148).
The class could get a boost if Summit pulls off an upcoming readout for ivonescimab in HARMONi-3, which features patients with first line NSCLC. A readout for a group of patients with squamous disease is due by the end of the year, marking a make-or-break moment for Summit. The company’s shares declined more than 13% to $12.20 in pre-market trading on Monday.
“HARMONi-3 now becomes even more important in establishing ivonescimab’s efficacy in NSCLC,” BMO wrote on Sunday.
The upcoming data could also address a key question the industry has been trying to answer since China became the go-to destination for drugs, particularly in oncology. The HARMONi-3 readout will be “the most important near-term test of whether the efficacy seen with PD-(L)1/VEGF agents in China translates into a global population and can clear an increasingly clear survival bar,” BMO said.

ROME — Italy has strongly denied a press report suggesting it opposes granting Germany partner status on the GCAP fighter program, claiming instead it fully backs German membership.
The unusually long rebuttal from the Italian ministry of defense followed a report in the Financial Times on Saturday that defense minister Guido Crosetto used a video conference call last week with other representatives of the Italian-UK-Japan fighter to oppose making Germany a member.
Berlin is mulling signing up to the program after the collapse of its talks with France to develop a rival sixth-generation jet.
The press report suggested Italy was pushing to hand Germany observer status on the program rather than full membership, although it did quote an Italian official saying German membership could follow.
Within hours of the report appearing, Crosetto’s ministry fired off a statement calling the article “entirely misleading”, adding it “does not reflect the position Italy has consistently maintained.”
The statement agreed that it wanted Germany to obtain observer status, but in order to accelerate full membership status, not to delay or block it.
“Italy has always expressed its full willingness to welcome Germany into the program. Indeed, precisely to facilitate and accelerate this process, Italy proposed that Germany joins as an observer, as an immediate, Program information-sharing enabler towards subsequent full membership,” it added.
The statement added, “This proposal was not intended to limit Germany’s future role in the program. Quite the opposite: it was designed to speed up the conditions for its involvement as quickly as possible, while safeguarding the program’s progress and established timetable.”
The talks come as the GCAP program picks up speed after the three nation partners handed a £4.6 billion ($6.1 billion) development contract to their national champions building the jet in July.
Rome has spent €875 million ($970 million) this year on development .
Canada has meanwhile already taken observer status on the program.
The Italian statement said, “It is therefore totally false any reporting on opposition to Germany’s participation. Italy has demonstrated, through its actions and proposals, that it considers Germany’s involvement a positive opportunity.”
It added, “Our priority remains ensuring that GCAP proceeds according to its agreed schedule, while creating the conditions for new partners to join through a clear and effective process. Italy is supporting, without delay, all the conditions to welcome Germany’s participation in the GCAP as soon as possible.”

EICMA 2026 • Here Are Some of the Serious and Obscure Brands That EICMA 2026 Had To Offer – Worth Knowing About
ZFFCN's New UK Plant To Supply Gasoline, Hybrid, and Electric Vehicle Axles to Bentley
13 photos
Photo: Bentley
Bentley is bringing a very important part of its vehicle assembly process closer to the British automaker's Crewe facility. ZF Foxconn Chassis Modules has started constructing a dedicated axle plant in Stoke-on-Trent, a facility that has been confirmed to supply a great deal of axles to the ultra-luxury automaker.
Production is scheduled to begin in 2027, and the ZFFCN axles in question are designed for a wide variety of vehicles. According to Bentley , the front and rear modules will support internal combustion, hybridized, and full-electric models. The Volkswagen Group-controlled manufacturer, however, did not mention any model whatsoever in the attached media release.
In any case, a joint venture that combines German chassis expertise with Taiwanese industrial capabilities is a truly interesting combo. The factory will occupy a site at Chatterley Park, which is approximately 17 miles (27 kilometers) from the Crewe headquarters. ZF Foxconn will assemble complete front and rear axle and suspension modules there.
Complete modules will be shipped to Crewe's production lines through a just-in-sequence manufacturing arrangement. In other words, a specific axle should arrive at Bentley's factory right before the corresponding vehicle reaches the relevant assembly station. The alternative would be axles that sit idly in inventory until somebody needs them, and this alternative isn't particularly efficient.
As implied, ZF Foxconn Chassis Modules brings Germany's ZF Friedrichshafen AG and Taiwan's Hon Hai Technology Group together. The partners completed the transaction that birthed the 50:50 joint venture in April 2024, with Foxconn acquiring half of ZF Chassis Modules GmbH.
Photo: Bentley In ZF Foxconn's own words, the company should be viewed as a full-service automotive manufacturing and logistics provider. It specializes in chassis systems, modules, and assemblies for both volume and premium automakers. As for its work, ZFFCN covers axle assembly, corner modules, supplier development, industrialization, quality management, and supply chain operations.
ZFFCN brings more than 30 years of experience in assembling axle systems and operating JIT and JIS production facilities. The biggest difference between just-in-time production and the JIS system is how the desired parts are presented to the contracting manufacturer. JIT means the parts are delivered to the production line when they are needed, while JIS delivers them when needed and in the exact assembly order required by the assembly line.
As of this writing, ZFFCN employs approximately 4,000 souls across 27 locations worldwide. The joint venture's experience should prove immensely useful at Crewe, where Bentley has to accommodate a growing number of powertrain technologies without creating one too many distinct supply arrangements for every model family.
Bentley's current lineup comprises four core models. The Continental GT, which can be had with a canvas top, is joined by the mechanically similar Flying Spur ultra-luxury sedan. The Bentayga is more than a Volkswagen Touareg with a nice suit, and the same can be said about the Porsche Cayenne Electric-derived Torcal electric sport utility vehicle.

Hyundai appears to be testing a new high-tech setup in the IONIQ 5 . A prototype was spotted with the door wide open, exposing a large display and a layout that looks very different from the current model.
Is Hyundai updating the IONIQ 5 with Pleos?
Is the IONIQ 5 next in line for an overhaul? Another mysterious IONIQ 5 test mule was recently caught in a parking garage in South Korea, revealing what’s rumored to be Hyundai’s software-defined vehicle (SDV).
Hyundai is betting heavily on software, AI, autonomous driving, robotics, and more as it expands from a traditional auto manufacturer to a “software-centric mobility leader.”
At the heart of it all is Hyundai Motor Group’s new Pleos Connect, an advanced in-vehicle infotainment and software platform.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Built on Android Automotive OS, Hyundai’s new setup features a larger, tablet-style infotainment screen with apps, split-screen views, and more. It’s similar to using a smartphone with an easier-to-use, customizable layout.
The Grandeur was the first to launch with Hyundai’s Pleos in Korea in May, followed by the IONIQ 3 in Europe. In the US, the new Tucson will be the first to go on sale with Pleos in early 2027.
Hyundai IONIQ 3 interior with Pleos Connect infotainment system (Source: Hyundai)
Is the IONIQ 5 next in line? Hyundai aims to launch its first SDV as early as next year, and the IONIQ 5 appears to be a contender.
An IONIQ 5 test car was captured again (shown below) by @JHS_spyshot_official in a Korean parking garage, but this time the door was wide open, offering a clear view of the new setup.
View this post on Instagram A post shared by JHS (@jhs_spyshot_official)
Hyundai appeared to be testing automated parking features, and as you can see, the setup is considerably different from the current IONIQ 5.
A large infotainment display sits at the center that appears to be running Hyundai Pleos, instead of the current dual 12.3″ screens. Meanwhile, the steering wheel and dash both appear to be completely redesigned.
Although it’s hard to see, previous spy images show the IONIQ 5 SDV test car with no driver display, with all information expected to move to the large center infotainment screen.
Hyundai Pleos Connect infotainment system (Source: Hyundai)
By 2030, Hyundai Motor Group plans to equip around 20 million Hyundai, Kia, and Genesis vehicles with the new Pleos setup.

Guess I'm holding onto my 2023 EV6 for as long as I can. I saw a preview of the new software and think it looks pretty solid, but I am NOT a fan of the "huge tablet" dashboard.

The only issue I have is the top of the steering wheel obscures the icons at the top of my driver's screen, but I'd rather have that than a giant hulking tablet sitting in the middle of the dash.

Over the summer, an IONIQ 6 prototype was spotted near Hyundai’s R&D hub in Europe with a similar high-tech setup.

source_document.body:
BMW opened its $700 million battery assembly plant in Woodruff, South Carolina last week and began building battery packs for the model iX5. The packs will travel 15 miles to BMW’s Spartanburg plant, where they’ll go into the first fully electric BMW built in the United States.
What’s Related
BMW plans to start assembling the iX5 in Spartanburg before the end of 2026 and put it on sale in the first quarter of 2027. The company expects to build at least six fully electric models at Spartanburg by 2030, with Woodruff supplying battery packs for future models as well.
The Woodruff plant is part of a $1.7 billion South Carolina investment BMW announced in 2022. The company put the other $1 billion into preparing its Spartanburg plant to build electric vehicles . Woodruff began regular battery pack production in November, ahead of the December start BMW had projected in July.
“With today’s opening of Plant Woodruff, we demonstrate how quickly we can scale a new battery concept to industrial production,” said Rich Everly, BMW’s vice president responsible for manufacturing at the Woodruff plant. Construction began in September 2023, equipment installation started a year later while crews were still working on the building, and the first test packs came off the line in summer 2025.
How Woodruff builds the packs
Woodruff buys cylindrical battery cells from outside suppliers and checks their voltage when they arrive. The cells go directly into the pack, eliminating the step of building separate battery modules. BMW says that design saves weight. The pack in the iX5 60 xDrive holds 144 kilowatt-hours of usable energy, the most of any fully electric BMW battery to date.
On the line, groups of cells are attached to coolers before they’re laser-cleaned and welded. Equipment checks each weld as it’s made, and foam holds the components in place inside the pack. After the housing is sealed, BMW installs the battery’s main control unit and inspects every finished pack before it leaves for Spartanburg.
How workers are being trained
BMW says more than 300 employees and about 250 robots work at Woodruff. Production employees practice on a virtual copy of the assembly line before using the equipment. BMW also used computer models of the plant to plan production before the line was ready to run.
During production, cameras and sensors collect data as the packs move down the line. BMW’s software analyzes that data and gives employees feedback while they work. The company uses the same system to check vehicle assembly at Spartanburg.
Where BMW gets its battery cells
BMW did not name the supplier for Woodruff’s first production packs. Four days before the opening, the automaker announced a deal with LG Energy Solution to buy cells made at existing U.S. plants starting in the late 2020s. BMW also signed Samsung SDI as an additional supplier of cells made in Europe.
“Diversifying procurement is an integral part of the BMW Group’s purchasing strategy,” said Nicolai Martin, the BMW board member responsible for purchasing. In Europe, the Samsung SDI deal will give BMW three suppliers making cells in the region, alongside CATL and EVE Energy.
Woodruff is the fourth plant to begin building BMW’s sixth-generation battery packs. Debrecen, Hungary, started in October 2025, followed by plants in Germany and China in October 2026. A fifth site in San Luis Potosí, Mexico , is due to start in 2027. BMW placed each pack plant close to a vehicle factory to shorten the trip from battery assembly to installation.

Osaka, Japan-headquartered Kansai Electric Power is acquiring a minority interest in Prospect Power Storage, a 150-MW/600-MWh battery energy storage system (BESS) owned by Elevate Infrastructure and ArcLight Capital Partners .
Elevate (a portfolio company of ArcLight) and ArcLight announced the deal on November 16. Prospect Power currently is the largest standalone BESS in commercial operation in the PJM Interconnection, the power grid operator that serves all or part of 13 states across the U.S. Mid-Atlantic and Midwest regions. Prospect Power is located in Rockingham County, Virginia.
The companies on Monday said the investment by Kansai is part of Elevate’s strategy “to develop and operate critical energy infrastructure at scale while attracting sophisticated long-term strategic capital.” The groups said the BESS is an important installation in an area with growing electricity demand driven by data centers, artificial intelligence, and electrification.
Utility-Scale Battery Energy Storage
“Prospect Power demonstrates Elevate’s ability to execute utility-scale battery storage projects from acquisition through commercial operation and deliver flexible capacity where the grid needs it most,” said Joshua Rogol, CEO of Elevate. “As electricity demand accelerates, projects like Prospect Power are increasingly important to strengthening grid reliability and supporting economic growth. We look forward to continuing to bring projects of this scale online across our portfolio.”
The groups said that Kansai’s investment “further expands the group of global strategic and institutional investors partnering with Elevate and ArcLight and reinforces the ability of the platform to combine deep energy infrastructure expertise, operational execution, and long-term capital.”
“Battery storage is becoming increasingly critical as energy demand grows and power markets require greater flexibility and reliability,” said Angelo Acconcia, managing partner of ArcLight. “Prospect Power demonstrates the value of bringing large-scale storage infrastructure into service in high-growth markets, and Kansai’s investment is a strong validation of both the quality of the asset and the growing need for storage as part of the nation’s power infrastructure.”
“Prospect Power is a high-quality operating asset in an important U.S. power market, and we are pleased to partner with Elevate and ArcLight through this investment – our first battery storage project outside Japan,” said Takayuki Doi, executive officer of Kansai’s Global Business. “We look forward to leveraging the experience gained through Prospect Power and exploring opportunities for further collaboration in battery storage and other energy infrastructure in the United States.”
Elevate brought Prospect Power into commercial operation in May of this year . The project is fully contracted under a 15-year power purchase agreement with Dominion Energy Virginia.

Levon Is a Quirky Skoolie That Serves as a Home Away From Home for Music-Loving Travelers
27 photos
Photo: Mobile Dwellings/YouTube screenshot
Old, decommissioned school buses turned into cozy, functional living spaces are one of the hottest trends in the realm of tiny living. With their sturdy construction, generous interior volume, and affordability compared to traditional RVs, these vehicles are seen by many as the perfect blank canvas for creating functional roving homes.
For many people, a school bus conversion is a practical way to create an affordable home on wheels, but for Dennis and Marty, it was an opportunity to turn a decades-old dream into reality and build something that echoes their personalities and everything they love about music, travel, and the freedom of the open road.
Dennis and Marty have built this quirky bus home nicknamed “Levon” not only to travel and explore new places but also to drive to music festivals all over the country. It has been their dream for 35 years. The idea of building a bus conversion first sparked in July of 1987, when Dennis attended a Grateful Dead concert in Eugene, Oregon, and saw a big converted bus that caught his attention. He then thought he had to have one of his own.
A couple of years ago, he and Marty decided it was time to make it happen. They bought a Thomas-built school bus that already had some work done to the interior and turned it into a colorful home for them and their dog, complete with an eclectic styling, plenty of unique custom features, and items that hold meaning to them.
Photo: Mobile Dwellings/YouTube screenshot They worked with a couple of professionals and a talented mural artist they met at a rest area to complete the conversion, and the result is a vibrant, full-of-character skoolie and a rolling tribute to the Grateful Dead, an American rock band formed in the 1960s known for their improvisational music.
From the get-go, they wanted their build to be much more than another ordinary skoolie, and indeed, the Levon is the kind of bus you can’t miss on the highway. The exterior immediately catches the eye with a lively color scheme that is entirely inspired by the Grateful Dead. The artist created a vibrant yet cohesive artwork on the bus’s body, with all kinds of things related to the band’s music, from a steam locomotive rolling down the tracks and Mount Hood to dancing bears and a Tumbledown Shack (Grateful Dead tribute band).
The interior of the bus is just as enchanting and full of personality, if not more. The couple wanted a comfortable living space , but they didn’t follow a conventional design, so everything you see inside is custom. With a bit of creativity, audacity, and a peculiar sense of style, they created a space that speaks of their love of music.
Photo: Mobile Dwellings/YouTube screenshot They used color, personal items, and an array of custom-made features to create a space where they are surrounded by things they love and that hold meaning to them. They also included every amenity they need for a comfortable life on the road.
The layout is simple and intuitive, and it flows easily from front to back with absolutely no separation walls between areas, not even for the bathroom facilities. As in many other conversions, the common, social areas occupy the front and middle of the bus, while the bathroom and sleeping quarters are toward the rear.
The entire interior is fitted with custom light blue cabinetry and furniture with lively orange cushions, and beautiful woodwork completes the design. The kitchen countertops, the dinette table, and overhead shelves are all made from live-edge natural wood, bringing a cozy, rustic touch to the space.
Photo: Mobile Dwellings/YouTube screenshot The bus still preserves most of its original windows, but they like to keep the colorful curtains drawn during the day. This doesn’t mean the interior is like a dark corridor, as the beautiful wooden ceiling is dotted by no fewer than seven skylights that bathe every area in natural light.
At the front, the couple installed a comfortable leather minivan seat with harnesses, and the driver’s area is full of trinkets that move when Levon is on the move. The living area includes a custom sofa with built-in storage, while the dinette boasts booth-style seating.
The kitchen is fully functional and provides the essentials for preparing meals, but Dennis and Marty say they do most of their cooking outdoors. For sleeping, they have a huge bed at the rear, while built-in closets on either side of the bus provide plenty of storage for clothes and personal belongings.
Photo: Mobile Dwellings/YouTube screenshot But the most remarkable area of the entire bus conversion is the bathroom. As mentioned, there are no walls to enclose this space, and its centerpiece is a gorgeous 1952 clawfoot bathtub, which has been given a unique makeover by a well-known Harley-Davidson tank painter.
Dennis and Marty’s love of music is reflected in many of the items they chose to decorate the interior. For instance, there are not one but two disco balls, one at the front and the other in the rear bedroom area. A drum set is also integrated on a raised section above a wheel well.
The couple doesn’t live in their bus conversion full time. Levon serves as their home away from home whenever they travel, especially when attending music festivals, but it could very well be a full-time home on wheels if they ever decide to adopt a nomadic lifestyle.
In terms of costs, Dennis and Marty paid about $67,000 for the conversion and invested another $15,000 in improvements. With the cost of the bus itself included, the project came to a total of about $90,000.

United Parcel Service has to temporarily replace a Boeing 767-300 freighter aircraft after sustaining damage when it was struck by the wing tip of a passenger plane during taxiing at Miami International Airport, complicating planning and operations with the peak season underway and volumes surging.
A UPS ( NYSE: UPS ) spokesperson declined to provide details about how UPS Airline operations will be impacted or how long the cargo jet will be out of service during a crucial period when every asset is needed to keep up with demand.
Integrated logistics companies like UPS typically have spare aircraft in reserve that can be substituted when a plane has a maintenance or other problem that prevents it from flying. A more likely scenario at this time of year would be for UPS to engage a third-party capacity provider to provide dedicated airlift until the 767 freighter can be repaired, or demand calms down.
The accident is expected to create operational headaches for UPS airline and logistics specialists, but likely won’t cause any delays for packages and freight.
The UPS cargo jet was involved in a low-speed ground collision at Miami Airport on Saturday night when Copa Airlines Flight 427, a Boeing 737-800 with 166 passengers that just touched down from Panama City, clipped the nose of the UPS aircraft with its left wing as it was taxiing to its gate and the UPS plane was preparing to depart for Bogotá, Colombia, according to the Federal Aviation Administration.
Air traffic control audio suggests the accident involved distracted driving. The FAA said air traffic controllers had instructed the UPS crew to give way to the Copa Airlines aircraft.
Copa pilot: “427, somebody hit us.”
ATC: “427, roger. UPS, you’re supposed to give way to the 73 there.”
UPS pilot: “Roger, we running checklist, runway change.”
ATC: “UPS 358, did you hit that aircraft?”
UPS pilot: “Yeah, we went too far, and then he clipped us with the wing.”
Photos of the UPS plane taken by passengers on the Copa jet and posted on social media show the nose crumpled, with a large hole in the panels.
🚨✈️ Here's a video showing the aftermath of a ground collision between a Copa Airlines Boeing 737 and a UPS Boeing 767 at Miami International Airport (MIA). The Copa aircraft's left wing struck the nose of the UPS jet at low speed near the intersection of two taxiways.… https://t.co/SbouQRRiOH pic.twitter.com/OPFDA4KjY4 — AirNav Radar (@AirNavRadar) November 15, 2026
Experts say it is challenging for pilots to judge clearance from the wingtips.
“From the seat, you can’t see your own wingtips. On a 737 they’re well behind you, and on a 767 or 777 they’re out of sight altogether. At night you judge another jet’s position by its lights, not its shape. Ground controllers sequence traffic but don’t guarantee wingtip separation. Clearance comes from airport design and the crew’s eyes, so a few feet of misjudgment at walking pace is enough,” said Helen Askew, a former 767 and 747 freighter captain and senior author, aviation at Travel Statistics Bureau (12,000+ flight hours, former airline Head of Flight Safety, who has flown both 767s and 747 freighters), explains how this can happen at walking pace.
The National Transportation Safety Administration has opened an investigation into the accident, which came two months after an Amazon 767 freighter operated by 21 Air overshot the runway at Miami and struck two vehicles, killing five people.
“We are aware of an incident involving one of our aircraft on the ground in Miami. Our crew is safe, and we are committed to working with authorities to determine what happened. The safety of our employees and the public is our highest priority,” UPS Airlines said in a statement posted on X.
The accident in Miami also occurred days after the one-year anniversary of the deadly crash of a UPS MD-11 freighter that suffered an engine detachment during takeoff.

source_document.body:
A Tesla Model Y left a parkway in El Dorado Hills, California, hit a tree and burst into flames in September, killing three of the four people inside. Tesla’s own report to federal regulators says Autopilot or “Full Self-Driving” was engaged, with the car doing 74 mph.
The crash was widely covered in the Sacramento area as a fiery single-car wreck. None of that coverage mentioned a driver-assist system. It’s the latest case in our ongoing investigation into fatal crashes hidden in Tesla’s NHTSA data .
What happened on Serrano Parkway
Late on Saturday, September 12, 2026, a 2024 Tesla Model Y with four people inside was heading west on Serrano Parkway, between Terracina Drive and Silva Valley Parkway. That’s a residential part of the Serrano community in El Dorado Hills, east of Sacramento.
According to the CHP’s Placerville office, the Model Y left the road “for unknown reasons,” hit a tree on the north side of the parkway, and caught fire. Officers got the call around 10:38 p.m. By the time they arrived, the car was fully engulfed in flames.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Charles Anthony Cameron, 30, of Sacramento, was thrown from the car and died at the scene. Alejandra Mendoza, 28, of Sacramento, and Kailauna Viola Mills, 28, of Roseville, were found dead inside once firefighters put out the fire. One of the two women was driving; CHP hasn’t publicly said which.
Mills lived in Arizona and was visiting family. Her uncle told CBS Sacramento she worked in the medical field and was supposed to get married next April.
A fourth person, a 28-year-old Sacramento woman, survived with major injuries.
CHP says the cause is still under investigation. Speed, impairment, and how the car left the road haven’t been released. And nobody has said a word about Autopilot.
What Tesla told the federal government
Under NHTSA’s Standing General Order, automakers have to report crashes where a Level 2 driver-assist system was engaged within 30 seconds of impact and someone is killed or hurt. Tesla filed a report on this one.
It lists a 2024 Model Y, a consumer vehicle, and marks the “Engagement Status” as “Verified Engaged.” That’s Tesla confirming through its own telematics that Autopilot or FSD was on. It logs a pre-crash speed of 74 mph , a fatality, and the California Highway Patrol as the investigating agency.
Then it redacts the narrative, the software version, and whether the road was inside the system’s operating domain, all as “confidential business information,” the same treatment Tesla gives 99.9% of its reports .
The rest of the report is strangely thin. Tesla lists the roadway type as “Unknown” and what the car hit as “Unknown,” even though police said it was a tree. It checks only one source for how it learned of the crash: the media. So Tesla found out about a triple-fatal crash in one of its cars from the news, then went into its own data and confirmed its driver-assist was on.
How we matched it: Tesla logged the incident time as 05:36 UTC, which is 10:36 p.m. Pacific on September 12, within two minutes of the 10:38 p.m. call CHP responded to. The city, the 2024 Model Y, the month, and the fatal outcome all line up. It’s the only fatal Tesla driver-assist report from El Dorado Hills in the data. It’s the same crash.
The fire
Two of the three victims were found inside the car after the fire was out. The survivor got out of, or was pulled from, the wreckage, depending on the report.
CHP hasn’t said whether the doors played any role, and we’re not suggesting they did. But it’s a fair question to ask about any Tesla crash with a fire, now that NHTSA is writing new rules for emergency door releases after years of complaints about people getting trapped. We’ve asked.
Electrek’s Take
This is the second triple-fatal crash in Tesla’s latest NHTSA filings where its driver-assist was verified engaged and the public never heard about it. The other one was on I-75 in Naples. Add Vineland and July’s four fatal crashes , and the pattern is hard to miss.
What stands out in this one is how little effort went into the report. Tesla knows the speed, knows the system was on, and has telematics. But it couldn’t fill in what the car hit, and it learned about three deaths in one of its cars from the news. Then it redacted the one field, the narrative, that would tell us what the car did.
Tesla wants regulators and customers to trust FSD with no one watching. That trust has to be earned with data. A company that seals the account of what its car did at 74 mph in a neighborhood, in a crash that killed three people, isn’t earning it.
We’re asking CHP Placerville whether its investigators knew the system was engaged, whether they got Tesla’s raw data or Tesla’s summary of it, and what they found about the fire and the doors. If CHP never got the full data, how will it ever determine the cause?
